title: Panic decision tree
description: A guided recovery for someone who has broken something and does not know what. One question at a time, plain language, large targets, no jargon in the questions themselves. The design constraint that shapes everything here: she is stressed, so she is not reading carefully, so every branch must state its cost before she can pick it.

symptom.description: How it looks from her side, not what it is called. 'My changes disappeared', not 'detached HEAD recovery'.

reassurance.description: Opens the tree. Honest, not soothing: if the work is almost certainly recoverable, say so and say why, because that is true of most git disasters and knowing it changes how carefully she proceeds.

backup_first.description: The command that makes the whole tree survivable, offered before the first question. Usually a backup branch. Nearly every git disaster is recoverable if a snapshot exists before the fix attempt.

root.description: Node key the tree starts at.

nodes.description: Keyed by node name. A node either asks a question with branches, or resolves with a fix.

ask.description: One question, plain language, answerable without knowing any git vocabulary.

how_to_tell.description: The command that answers the question for her when she cannot tell. She often does not know which branch she is on, and that is the normal case, not a failure.

goto.description: Another node key, or a terminal node.

resolve.description: A terminal node. Present instead of `branches`.

destroys.description: Required whenever anything is lost. Stated before she runs it, in the same view as the button. 'Nothing' is a valid and reassuring answer.

verify.description: How she confirms it worked. Without this she cannot tell recovery from further breakage, which is the worst moment to be uncertain.
